articles.title: Chuva em Tupã e Promissão causa estragos e destrói festival | G1
articles.standfirst: Chuva e ventos de até 50 km/h, na manhã deste domingo (31) também causaram alagamentos, quedas de árvores e destelhamentos em Tupã, Cafelândia e Guaiçara (SP).
articles.summary: Temporal com ventos fortes atingiu Tupã e Promissão, destruindo a estrutura do Festival do Folclore e causando quedas de energia e alagamentos na região.
articles.body:
As rajadas causaram quedas de energia e pontos de alagamento nos bairros Jardim São João e Jardim do Lago. Segundo a prefeitura, não houve registro de feridos ou desalojados.

O Estádio Municipal Verano Piromalli foi a estrutura mais atingida. A cobertura da arquibancada e o telhado do vestiário desabaram com a força do vento.

Além do estádio, quatro escolas municipais sofreram danos. Na Escola Professora Aurélia Moreira de Barros, a força da ventania arrancou a cobertura da quadra.

Por causa dos estragos, as aulas foram totalmente suspensas na Escola Professora Aurélia Moreira de Barros e em outras duas unidades, nesta segunda-feira (31), enquanto uma quarta escola cancelou as atividades apenas no período da manhã.

Estádio ficou danificado devido à chuva — Foto: Vanderlei dos Santos

O temporal que atingiu a região durante o fim de semana também provocou transtornos em outros municípios do centro-oeste paulista.

Em Tupã (SP), a força do vento destruiu a estrutura da 5ª edição do Festival do Folclore (Fefolt), montada na Praça da Bandeira. Como as apresentações haviam sido encerradas no sábado (29), o local tinha pouco movimento no momento da tempestade e ninguém ficou ferido.

A tempestade também atingiu Cafelândia (SP), onde o bairro Vila Belém foi um dos pontos mais afetados.

A chuva forte da noite de domingo (30) provocou estragos em estrutura de festival de Tupã (SP) — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Equipes municipais atuaram no atendimento a ocorrências relacionadas a falhas no fornecimento de energia, destelhamentos e remoção de galhos e entulhos espalhados pelas vias públicas. Não houve registro de desalojados.

Já em Guaiçara (SP), foram registradas quedas de árvores, muros derrubados e residências destelhadas.

A Defesa Civil, o Fundo Social, servidores municipais e equipes da CPFL se mobilizaram para atender as ocorrências nas áreas mais críticas.

articles.title: 'Haiwaan' director Priyadarshan reveals Saif Ali Khan almost starred in 'Garam Masala'; recalls wanting to meet Tiger Pataudi
articles.summary: Priyadarshan recalled how Saif Ali Khan nearly became part of 'Garam Masala'. The filmmaker also shared an interesting story about his first meeting w.
articles.body: Priyadarshan recalled how Saif Ali Khan nearly became part of 'Garam Masala'. The filmmaker also shared an interesting story about his first meeting with Saif Ali Khan. Their conversation, however, was not initially about cinema. Priyadarshan was more interested in meeting Saif Ali Khan's father, legendary cricketer Mansur Ali Khan Pataudi. The director recently opened up about his long association with Saif Ali Khan. He also spoke about his admiration for Tiger Pataudi. Priyadarshan's memories of the former Indian cricket captain eventually became a recurring topic during the making of 'Haiwaan'.Saif Ali Khan could have starred in 'Garam Masala'Priyadarshan revealed that Saif Ali Khan was once considered for 'Garam Masala'. The director had met the actor with the intention of narrating the story. However, the film's screenplay was not completed in time.“I had gone to meet Saif to narrate the story of Garam Masala," he told News 18. Writer Neeraj Vora was still working on the complete script at the time. Saif Ali Khan waited for three days. The screenplay was still not ready. He eventually committed his dates to another project. “He couldn’t do the film. Neeraj (Vora; writer) couldn’t finish writing the entire script. Saif waited for three days, but Neeraj couldn’t take the complete script to him. As a result, he gave the dates to somebody else," Priyadarshan says. The film eventually went ahead with Akshay Kumar and became one of the popular comedies of its time.Priyadarshan's first question to Saif Ali KhanPriyadarshan's first meeting with Saif Ali Khan had another memorable detail. The filmmaker was a huge admirer of Mansur Ali Khan Pataudi. He had followed the cricketer's career closely. Meeting his son allowed Priyadarshan to ask about him. "The first thing that I told him was, ‘Is your father here? I want to meet him.'" Priyadarshan's admiration for Tiger Pataudi went back to his own younger days. He remembered watching the former Indian captain play. He also recalled an unsuccessful attempt to meet him.The cricket memory Priyadarshan still remembersPriyadarshan recalled seeing Tiger Pataudi during a Ranji Trophy match. The cricketer was representing Hyderabad at the time. “I remember him playing Ranji Trophy at the university stadium," Priyadarshan remembers fondly. The filmmaker then described how he once tried to find Tiger Pataudi at the stadium. His attempt ended with an injury instead of a meeting. “He was playing for Hyderabad. I wanted to find him and meet him, and I ran with all my might and had a big fall. I got a huge injury and couldn’t meet him. Later, I remember watching him play in Chennai against West Indies. Garfield Sobers’ team was playing at that time. This was the same match where Farokh Engineer scored a hundred. I had just started playing at that time," he added. Priyadarshan also played competitive cricket during his youth. His sporting ambitions ended after a serious eye injury.Tiger Pataudi became a topic during 'Haiwaan'Priyadarshan and Saif Ali Khan have now finally worked together on 'Haiwaan'. Their conversations on the sets often returned to Tiger Pataudi. “On the sets, I discussed Tiger Pataudi with Saif a lot. I remember all his scores. I took the book that Saif had signed for me. It was on Tiger Pataudi," he shared. The filmmaker's knowledge of Tiger Pataudi's career helped create a personal connection with Saif Ali Khan. Their discussions also brought back Priyadarshan's memories of following Indian cricket.Saif Ali Khan and Akshay Kumar reunite in 'Haiwaan''Haiwaan' brings Saif Ali Khan and Akshay Kumar together after 18 years. The two actors previously shared screen space in 'Tashan'. Saif Ali Khan plays a visually challenged protagonist. 'Haiwaan' is scheduled to release theatrically on September 11. articles.body: Sunny Deol is back on set, picking up where he left off on Antony after wrapping his commitments to 'Batwara 1947'. The actor has begun the next schedule of the upcoming cop thriller, with the current leg of filming focused entirely on high-octane action sequences.Sunny Deol resumes 'Antony's shootAccording to a Mid-Day report, the latest schedule for 'Antony' kicked off at Film City on August 26, with Sunny shooting extensive action portions for the film. articles.body: A film that opened with barely any fanfare has quietly become one of the year's most unexpected box office stories. articles.body: Yash-starrer ‘Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups’ enters its first Monday with its sights firmly set on the next major domestic milestones. The Geetu Mohandas directorial opened with a staggering Rs. 101.10 crore net in India and has maintained a strong pace through its first five days. With the film already crossing Rs. 285 crore in worldwide gross collections, the first Monday will be crucial in determining how strongly it holds after the opening weekend, shifting towards its next domestic benchmarks. The immediate target is to strengthen its hold during the first week before eyeing the Rs. 225 crore and eventually Rs. 250 crore India net milestones.'Toxic' has already strengthened its commercial credentials by surpassing 'Dhurandhar Part 1's reported opening-day India net collection. The bigger challenge now, since its release on August 26 has been converting the debut into a sustained theatrical run amid the strong mixed reactions across social media platforms.Toxic Movie Review'Toxic' Day 1 to Day 5 earnings'Toxic' announced its arrival with an extraordinary Rs. 101.10 crore net on Day 1 from 24,579 shows. Its India gross stood at Rs. 120.75 crore, while the overseas market contributed Rs. 20 crore, taking the worldwide gross for the opening day to Rs. 140.75 crore.The film saw a natural correction on Day 2 but still added a sizeable Rs. 37.65 crore net from 22,629 shows. Its India net collection reached Rs. 138.75 crore, with the domestic gross at Rs. 165.85 crore. Day 3 brought another Rs. 27.20 crore net, taking the cumulative India net to Rs. 165.95 crore and India gross to Rs. 198.10 crore.The film then added Rs. 25.15 crore on Day 4, followed by Rs. 23 crore on Day 5. Based on the day-wise figures provided, its India net total stood at Rs. 214.10 crore after Day 5. With another Rs. 0.68 crore coming in on Day 6 so far, the running India net total has reached Rs 214.78 crore.The Yash-led film opened internationally with Rs. 20 crore on Day 1. Overseas earnings increased its worldwide opening-day gross to Rs. 140.75 crore when combined with the domestic business. On Day 2, the film added another Rs. 8 crore overseas, taking the reported international gross to Rs. 24.25 crore at that stage. The film subsequently added Rs. 3.50 crore overseas on Day 3. At the end of Day 5, the overseas gross stood at Rs. 29.25 crore, pushing the worldwide gross collection to Rs. 285.20 crore.'Toxic' Day 6 collection live trackingAs per Sacnilk's live tracking, Toxic is currently running across 9,368 shows on Day 6, having collected Rs. 4.03 crore net so far.This takes the film's total India gross collection to Rs. 260.71 crore and its India net total to Rs. 218.13 crore, with final numbers for the day still awaited.The current language-wise figures include Rs. 2.43 crore from Hindi, Rs. 1.13 crore from Kannada and Rs. 35 lakh from Telugu and Rs. 12 lakh from Tamil.Day wise collections for 'Toxic'Day 1: Rs. 101.10 croreDay 2: Rs. 37.65 croreDay 3: Rs. 27.20 croreDay 4: Rs. 25.15 croreDay 5: Rs. 23.00 croreDay 6 [LIVE]: Rs. 4.03 croreTOTAL: Rs. 218.13 croreMore about 'Toxic'Directed by Geetu Mohandas, 'Toxic' is a gangster drama centred on Raya, played by Yash, unfolding against the backdrop of Portuguese-era Goa. The story traces Raya's rise within the criminal underworld, his bond with his sister Ganga, and his complicated relationships with the women in his life. Yash takes on a dual role, playing both Raya and his son Ticket. Nayanthara plays Ganga, Kiara Advani features as Nadia, and Rukmini Vasanth plays Mellisa, with Huma Qureshi, Akshay Oberoi and Tara Sutaria rounding out the supporting cast in significant roles. The CBFC cleared the film with an 'A' certificate, making it an adults-only theatrical release.'Toxic's content has continued to draw scrutiny even as its box office run remains strong. The film's depiction of violence and treatment of women has attracted criticism, including from former BJP leader K Annamalai, whose remarks have reportedly prompted broader discussions within the CBFC about how extreme on-screen violence should be assessed going forward. Despite this ongoing debate, the film's commercial performance has continued largely unaffected.DISCLAIMER: The box office numbers and data in this article are compiled from diverse public and industry sources. articles.title: Shakira explica por qué eligió Madrid para su residencia: “Es una ciudad que celebra la inmigración latina”
articles.standfirst: La cantante colombiana habla de “hispanidad” en una tribuna en el periódico El País
articles.summary: La cantante colombiana habla de “hispanidad” en una tribuna en el periódico El País
articles.body: El Mundo Macondo, o más conocido como el estadio Shakira, reunirá a más de 600.000 personas en los 12 conciertos que la cantante colombiana dará en este recinto que ha levantado en Madrid. Con motivo de ello, la artista ha escrito una columna en el periódico El País en el que defiende la inmigración latina, muestra su amor a Madrid y manda un mensaje a Donald Trump. Shakira ha confesado en esta tribuna que eligió Madrid por su relación estrecha con sus compatriotas: “Es una ciudad en la que la inmigración latina no se tolera, se celebra”. "España la ha abrazado, y ese abrazo la ha hecho más joven, más pujante, más creativa. Compartimos lengua, memoria, gestos, sobremesas. El Atlántico, entre nosotros, dejó de ser un océano hace mucho tiempo. Es un lazo. De Madrid se dice que quien no es de ningún lado es de aquí", asegura. En sus primeras líneas, Shakira lanza un mensaje a Donald Trump por su política de expatriación de latinos: "Frente a eso, la rabia es legítima. Pero yo elegí responder con una celebración: la más grande que fuéramos capaces de imaginar". A lo largo de las líneas escritas en El País, Shakira también hace un llamamiento para cambiar conceptos. "Hablemos de latinidad, un abrazo todavía más amplio. La hispanidad es hermosa, pero se queda corta para todo lo que somos. El español es latino; el portugués, el italiano y el francés también". "Y todos los latinoamericanos somos latinos. Brasil, el país más grande de América Latina, no habla español, habla portugués. La hispanidad no alcanza a abrazarlo; la latinidad sí. Somos una nación sin fronteras que lleva cinco siglos construyéndose: la mezcla de África, América y el sur de Europa. No juzgo con la mirada de hoy a los humanos de hace quinientos años; me quedo con lo que somos: una fusión que es nuestra riqueza", sentencia la cantante. Macondo Park es un recinto temático diseñado en Madrid para albergar la residencia de 12 conciertos de Shakira en su gira ‘Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran World Tour.’ Este proyecto, que se encuentra en el Espacio Iberdrola Music entre Villaverde y Getafe, cuenta con 15 hectáreas con el que la cantante Shakira quiere batir récords en nuestra ciudad congregando a 50.000 personas cada noche desde el 18 de septiembre al 11 de octubre de 2026. Está inspirado en la literatura colombiana y la cultura latina, funciona como un parque temático con música, arte, moda y gastronomía. En él se diferencian 8 áreas que incluyen escenarios secundarios, zonas VIP, fan zones y espacios culturales. Así como un ‘espacio Macondito’ destinado a los más pequeños.

articles.title: Meep, meep. ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ opens with $15.5 million, ‘Spider-Man’ stays No. 1 for fifth weekend
articles.summary: NEW YORK — Three years after Warner Bros.
articles.body: NEW YORK — Three years after Warner Bros. abruptly canned “Coyote vs. Acme,” the Looney Tunes feature film that was given a new lease on life by Ketchup Entertainment debuted with an estimated $15.5 million in ticket sales over the weekend. For the fifth weekend in a row, “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” topped the North American box office. It grossed $22.2 million in U.S. and Canadian theaters, according to studio estimates Sunday, bringing its worldwide total to $2.33 billion and making it the fourth highest-grossing film of all time. “Coyote vs. Acme,” which had been relegated to the dust heap, fared best of the newcomers, debuting in second place. The Ridley Scott action drama “The Dog Stars,” starring Jacob Elordi, flopped. The film, about a pilot and German Shepherd who survive a global pandemic, opened in fifth place with $8 million for 20th Century Studios. It added $11.3 million overseas, a poor result for a film that cost between $70 million and $100 million to make. “Coyote vs. Acme,” however, scored a decent, hard-earned opening. In 2023, Warner Bros. canceled any release of the completed film, preferring to take a tax write off on a movie originally produced for its streaming service, HBO Max. Warner also shelved “Batgirl” and “Scoob! Holiday Haunt,” both of which remain unreleased. “Coyote vs. Acme,” based on an Ian Frazier “Shouts and Murmurs” New Yorker column, is about Wile E. Coyote suing the Acme Corporation for its faulty products. It stars Will Forte, John Cena, Lana Condor and Eric Bauza. The film, a hybrid of live-action and animation directed by Dave Green, cost $70 million to make. But despite good test screening scores, Warner Bros. opted to ax the completed film. After an outcry, the studio put the film up for sale. Early last year, Ketchup Entertainment acquired worldwide distribution rights for about $50 million. For the makers of the film, just getting released was a victory. “’Coyote vs. Acme’ is finally, gloriously, in theaters now,” Green said on social media Friday. “Which means one thing. WE WON.” Reviews and audience scores were also good. Moviegoers gave it an “A” CinemaScore. Critics were just as enthusiastic. On Rotten Tomatoes, it rated 95% fresh. While the result might have counted as a disappointment for some $70 million movies, the opening weekend for “Coyote vs. Acme” was the best ever for Ketchup. The indie distributor’s previous high was 2024’s “The Day the Earth Blew Up” (a $3.1 million opening), another Warner-made Looney Tunes castoff. “The box office numbers are fair, but the reception is excellent and the release should set up good ancillary business for kids’ viewing, where the film should recoup its investment,” said David A. Gross, who publishes the box office newsletter FranchiseRe. “The Odyssey,” in its seventh weekend, slid to third place with $14.3 million. It remains unusually strong overseas, where the Christopher Nolan movie grossed $48.6 million over the weekend. Altogether, the Universal Pictures release has collected $1.55 billion in global sales. Top 10 movies by domestic box office With final domestic figures being released Monday, this list factors in the estimated ticket sales for Friday through Sunday at U.S. and Canadian theaters, according to Rentrak: 1. “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” $22.2 million. 2. “Coyote vs. Acme,” $15.5 million. 3. “The Odyssey,” $14.3 million. 4. “Insidious: Out of the Further,” $10.1 million. 5. “The Dog Stars,” $8 million. 6. “Buddy,” $5.4 million. 7. “The End of Oak Street,” $5 million. 8. “PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie,” $4.9 million. 9. “Mutiny,” $2.8 million. 10. “Tony,” $2.2 million.

The host mentioned Ranbir Kapoor, Ranveer Singh and Sidharth Malhotra. Responding to the question, Kapoor said, “Naa shakal se jaanta hu, naa personally jaanta hu; woh mere samne aajaye toh mujhe pata bhi nahi hai…”Kapoor went on to clarify that he does not follow their work closely.“Woh kaun hai mujhe maalum bhi nahi hai. Ranbir toh Rishi Kapoor ka ladka hai na… isiliye main jaanta hu… aur baaki… maine kabhi unka kaam kabhi dekha nahi hai, kaise bolte hai, kaise khade hote hai, mujhe kya pata ki kya baat karte hai,” he said.Kapoor’s comments suggest that his familiarity with Ranbir stems primarily from the actor’s family background, rather than from having closely followed his filmography.Annu Kapoor questions criticism of successful starsDuring the conversation, Kapoor was also asked about situations where veteran actors such as Naseeruddin Shah have made critical observations about major stars including Shah Rukh Khan and Amitabh Bachchan.Responding to the broader idea of established actors commenting on successful stars, Kapoor questioned why criticism is often directed at people who have already achieved significant popularity.“Jab bhi bologe, nakaratmak hi bologe. Iss country mein tumhe bhi aham bolne wale bahut log hain, ki tum aham actor ho. Unke drishtikon se satya kuch nahi ho jata,” he said.Kapoor further pointed out that it is audiences who ultimately determine which actors become stars.“Janta ne toh unko superstars banaya hai. Woh inn successful star ke baare mein hi kyun bolte hain?” he added.His comments appeared to emphasise the distinction between an individual’s personal opinion and the larger public perception of an actor’s popularity and success.Annu Kapoor’s perspective on contemporary BollywoodKnown for his outspoken views and decades-long association with Hindi cinema, Annu Kapoor has frequently discussed the changing nature of the film industry. His latest remarks offer an insight into his relatively limited engagement with the work of some younger Bollywood actors. While Ranbir Kapoor, Ranveer Singh and Sidharth Malhotra are among the prominent names of contemporary Hindi cinema, Kapoor made it clear that he does not closely follow their careers or films.Annu Kapoor’s latest filmOn the work front, Annu Kapoor was most recently seen in 'Uttar Da Puttar'. The film also features Rukhsar Rehman, Brijendra Kala, Pavan Malhotra, Ishtiyak Khan and Jeeveshu Ahluwalia. articles.title: Melinda French Gates stuns festival crowd, pledges to match Olivia Rodrigo's fundraising for $20M haul
articles.summary: Melinda French Gates pledged to match every donation at Olivia Rodrigo's Daisy Chain Fields festival, doubling the fundraising total to $20 million.
articles.body: Olivia Rodrigo introduced Daisy Chain Fields festival attendees to a surprise guest with a huge heart. After revealing that her inaugural music festival raised $10 million for various women-focused nonprofits, the "drivers license" singer revealed a shocking fundraising update. Before her headlining set at the event in Irvine, Rodrigo announced that Melinda French Gates would match every donation to the dollar, for a grand total of $20 million fundraised. Rodrigo, who announced her first female-driven festival in June, told the crowd that she was "grateful" for each of the booked acts who performed "for free" throughout the day as she celebrated her initial $10 million fundraising effort. "I really believe that giving women the tools to decide their own futures and live healthy lives free of violence and discrimination is the most effective tool we have at changing the world for the better," Rodrigo said. "And I don’t know many people who represent that idea more than Melinda French Gates." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE The former Disney Channel actress admitted that Gates was "one of the most inspiring women I've ever met," while championing her dedication to "empowering women and girls that might have otherwise been forgotten." "She's generous and brave and has done so much good in this world, and I’m totally floored because, as well as being in attendance here tonight, she’s pledged to double every dollar that we made here today to a grand total of funds being donated to $20 million," Rodrigo told the crowd. "I'm so grateful!" "Look at what you have done," Gates told Rodrigo after joining the "good 4 u" singer on stage. "Look at what you created!" "What I love about you is that you know that real power is not up here on stage, it's with everybody there, all of you," Gates continued. "When women and girls come together to dream and to lead, we change the world." The former wife of Microsoft founder Bill Gates added, "And, so long after the lights go down from this festival, the organizations doing this work will keep doing it because you all are here, so thank you for being here and thank you, Olivia."
